clue.text: Vegetable produced by merry old soul

parts.note: to bore fruit or children is to have produced them
Old King Cole of the nursery rhyme was a merry old soul

explanation.surface: A vegetable grown, it seems, by a jolly elderly person.
explanation.walkthrough: Old King Cole is the 'merry old soul' of an English nursery rhyme.
explanation.definitionFit: Borecole is an old name for kale, a leafy green cabbage.

clue.text: Rob the bent and the result's trouble!

indicators.note: bent means twisted out of shape, so the letters are reshuffled

explanation.surface: Steal from the corrupt and you'll end up in difficulty.
explanation.definitionFit: Bother means fuss or difficulty, a nuisance.

clue.text: Think logically about a certain issue

parts.note: re means about, concerning
a son is a particular kind of issue, or offspring

explanation.surface: Reflect rationally on a particular question.
explanation.walkthrough: 'issue' reads as a topic for debate; here it means offspring.
explanation.definitionFit: To reason is to work things out by logical thought.

clue.text: Once in an American state, hush up!

indicators.note: in shows one piece placed inside the abbreviation for the state

parts.note: Cal is an abbreviation for California

explanation.surface: Someone in the US is told to keep quiet.
explanation.definitionFit: To conceal a scandal is to keep it secret, to cover it up.

clue.text: Advance due to the demise of the left?

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for left
demise is death, the end

explanation.surface: Is progress the result of the political left's collapse?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Advance' looks like progress; it is a verb, to loan money.
explanation.definitionFit: To advance money is to lend it ahead of time.

clue.text: To prosecute with the exertion of some pull

parts.note: to prosecute a war or campaign is to wage it

explanation.surface: Taking legal action against someone with a bit of influence behind you.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prosecute' suggests the courts, but here it is the sense of carrying on a campaign, as in waging war.
explanation.definitionFit: Towage is the act or charge of hauling a vessel by rope, an effort of pulling.

clue.text: More than fifty pound divided by a general

indicators.note: divided by means a letter splits the other run of letters apart

parts.note: over means more than
L is the Roman numeral for fifty
L (from libra) is the abbreviation for a pound

explanation.surface: Over fifty pounds shared out by an army officer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'divided by' looks like arithmetic; it puts A between OVER and LL.
explanation.definitionFit: Overall means taking everything into account, comprehensive.

clue.text: Avoids sailors — it's an affectation

parts.note: ABs are able seamen, sailors

indicators.note: an affectation is something put on or contrived, signalling these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Seamen shun something pretentious.
explanation.definitionFit: To abstain is to refrain from doing something, such as voting or drinking.

clue.text: Coffee-making directions newsmen love to follow

parts.note: E is east, a compass direction
S is south, another compass direction
the press is journalists collectively
love is zero in tennis, shaped like O

explanation.surface: Journalists like to follow the instructions for brewing coffee.
explanation.definitionFit: Espresso is a method of brewing strong coffee by forcing steam through grounds.

clue.text: Seeing a fall in sound instruction

indicators.note: in tells us one piece sits inside the other here

parts.note: a ting is a light ringing sound
rain is a fall from the sky

explanation.surface: Watching someone tumble during a noisy lesson.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Seeing' is a link meaning 'given'. 'Fall' tempts as a tumble; it is a fall of rain.
explanation.definitionFit: Training is teaching or coaching given to a learner.

clue.text: Begins making party drink

parts.note: a set is a group or party of people
to sup is to drink, sip

explanation.surface: Someone starts making a drink for a party.
explanation.definitionFit: To set up a business is to start or establish it.

clue.text: Mounting anger after French wine proves acidic stuff

indicators.note: after puts the reversed anger piece behind the wine

parts.note: vin is French for wine

indicators.note: mounting means going upward, so in a down answer the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: rage is anger

explanation.surface: Fury rising after the French wine turns out sour.
explanation.definitionFit: Vinegar is a sour liquid made by fermenting wine, used as a condiment.

clue.text: Summons the first lady's about to endorse

indicators.note: about here means the first lady's name goes round the other piece

parts.note: Eve was the first woman in the Bible; her possessive gives EVES
to OK something is to endorse or approve it

explanation.surface: The President's wife calls people together, ready to give her approval.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First lady' suggests a president's wife, but it is Eve, the first woman.
explanation.definitionFit: To evoke is to call up or conjure, as a spirit is called forth.

clue.text: Address a man of the cloth will give

definitions.text: Address a man of the cloth will give

parts.words: Address a man of the cloth will give
parts.note: the home address a parish clergyman would write down is his official residence

explanation.surface: A priest's speech, or the place where he lives?
explanation.definitionFit: A vicarage is the house provided for a parish priest, so it is where he lives.

clue.text: Walked a horse around very quietly

indicators.note: around means the horse surrounds the other letters

parts.note: a steed is a horse
pp is pianissimo, very quiet in music

explanation.surface: Someone led a horse gently around.
explanation.definitionFit: To have stepped is to have walked, moving by paces.

clue.text: They offer support to those people pegging out

definitions.text: They offer support to those people pegging out

parts.words: They offer support to those people pegging out
parts.note: pegging out sounds like dying, but it is pinning washing to cords in the garden to dry

explanation.surface: Helpers comfort the dying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pegging out' is slang for dying; here it means hanging washing up with pegs.
explanation.definitionFit: Garments are hung on cords with pegs to dry, and the cords hold them up.

clue.text: As usual, a position for a hanger-on

parts.note: par is the normal level, as in 'on par'
a site is a location or position

explanation.surface: Typically, a place for a groupie.
explanation.definitionFit: A parasite is someone who lives off others, a sponger.

clue.text: Dissipated girl put in prison

parts.note: miss is a girl or young woman
pent means penned up, confined

explanation.surface: A wayward young woman is jailed.
explanation.definitionFit: Misspent and dissipated both describe time or money squandered wastefully.

clue.text: The parson is a potentially great comic dramatist

indicators.note: potentially says these letters could become something else when rearranged

explanation.surface: A clergyman might turn out to be a fine comic playwright.
explanation.definitionFit: Aristophanes was the leading comic playwright of ancient Athens, author of The Frogs.

clue.text: A seaport in great chaos

indicators.note: chaos means disorder, so the letters are thrown into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A harbour town in a terrible mess.
explanation.definitionFit: Tangier is a port city in Morocco on the Strait of Gibraltar.

clue.text: For the viewers this is a wash-out!

definitions.text: For the viewers this is a wash-out!

parts.words: For the viewers this is a wash-out!
parts.note: the viewers are eyes, and the wash-out is a rinse for them, not a flop

explanation.surface: Audiences find the show a complete failure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wash-out' suggests a flop; read literally, it is something that rinses out the eyes.
explanation.definitionFit: An eye bath is a small cup used to rinse the eyes clean.

clue.text: Environmentally concerned English writer

parts.note: green describes ecological concerns

explanation.surface: An eco-minded English author.
explanation.definitionFit: Graham Greene was an English novelist, author of Brighton Rock.

clue.text: Recent change of heart

indicators.note: change of tells us the following word has its letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone has had a recent change of heart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'change of' rearranges RECENT; 'heart' is the definition, not part of the phrase 'change of heart'.
explanation.definitionFit: The centre of something is its heart or core.

clue.text: Get the fool to come in — he's quite agreeable

parts.note: an ass is a fool
to enter is to come in

explanation.surface: Invite the idiot inside: he's a nice enough chap.
explanation.definitionFit: One who assents agrees, so an assenter is a person who goes along with things.

clue.text: Name some judge or general

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Pick any title: a judge, perhaps, or a general.
explanation.definitionFit: George is a common given name, borne by six British kings.

clue.text: Goddess having hot time

parts.note: H is short for hot, as on a tap
an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: A deity enjoying herself in the heat.
explanation.definitionFit: Hera was queen of the Greek gods, wife of Zeus.

clue.text: One with nicer disposition and so peace-loving

parts.note: the Roman numeral I is one

indicators.note: disposition, an arranging, says the letters of nicer are set out afresh

explanation.surface: Someone with a pleasanter temperament is therefore calm and gentle.
explanation.definitionFit: Irenic describes something aimed at reconciliation, favouring harmony over conflict.

clue.text: Declining to be reasonable about sales-pitch

indicators.note: about means the word for reasonable is wrapped round the other piece

parts.note: decent means acceptable, reasonable
an ad is an advertisement, a pitch to sell

explanation.surface: Refusing to be sensible when hearing a salesman out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Declining' reads as refusing, but it is falling into decay.
explanation.definitionFit: Decadent means in moral or cultural decline, degenerating from a better state.

clue.text: The whole country absorbs conservationists

indicators.note: absorbs means the country takes the other piece inside it

parts.note: Eire is the Irish name for Ireland
NT is the National Trust, the UK heritage conservation charity

explanation.surface: An entire nation takes in environmental campaigners.
explanation.definitionFit: Entire means complete, with nothing missing.

clue.text: Expensive material obtained for ready money only

parts.note: cash is ready money
mere means only, nothing more than

explanation.surface: Luxurious fabric can be had just for cash.
explanation.definitionFit: Cashmere is a fine, costly wool from Kashmir goats, made into cloth.
